items.exemplar:
A. The transcontinental railroad, completed at Promontory Summit in 1869, let settlers, cattle, and wheat move cheaply across the continent, knitting the West to eastern markets.

B. The Homestead Act (1862) offered 160 acres of public land to settlers, drawing hundreds of thousands of farms onto the Plains.

C. Native peoples resisted fiercely: the Sioux destroyed Custer's command at Little Bighorn (1876), and the Ghost Dance movement sought spiritual renewal against white expansion before it was crushed at Wounded Knee (1890).
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE way American settlement rapidly transformed the West in the 25 years after the Civil War.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND such transformation.
C. Briefly explain ONE way Native Americans resisted American settlement in this period.
items.stimulus: The 1869 photograph of the Golden Spike ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah, shows two locomotives nose to nose, surrounded by celebrating workers and officials — the moment the continent was joined by rail.
